title: refactor: UI asset extraction
desiredOutcome: The 5,340 embedded CSS/JS lines live as real, editor-highlightable files under scripts/ui/ (no .py ever, pinned by a selftest), read at import with explicit utf-8 and assembled byte-identically into the same UI_HTML/_CSS/_SCRIPT constants — every substring pin and both Playwright checks pass untouched, and the served page stays one self-contained HTML file.
summary: The 5,340 embedded CSS/JS lines are real files under scripts/ui/ - panel.html/css/js and report.css/js - assembled at import by _panel_ui and _report_ui into the exact same constants, proven byte-identical old-vs-new (UI_HTML 244588; _CSS 61698; _SCRIPT 37708). panel-server.py fell 8287 -> 4521 lines and render-report.py 4587 -> 3024 before any Python split. Every existing pin passed untouched, both Playwright checks green, scripts/ui pinned .py-free from both modules, and the docs plus CONTRIBUTING now state the layout invariant. The desired outcome holds verbatim. One trap found and dodged: extracting a non-raw literal from source text captures pre-escape bytes; the report extractor reads the evaluated AST constant instead.

tasks.title: Panel: ui/panel.{html,css,js} + _panel_ui.raw_template()
tasks.description: Split the UI_HTML r-string at its natural seams: CSS (keeps /*__THEME_TOKENS__*/), JS (keeps every __*__ placeholder), HTML skeleton. _panel_ui.raw_template() reads the three assets utf-8 and returns the exact pre-substitution string; panel-server sets UI_HTML = _panel_ui.raw_template() and the .replace() substitution block is untouched. A logic-free move: all ~401 pins must pass unmodified in the same commit. A failing pin means the bytes moved — fix the move, never the pin.

add: _panel_ui: placeholders present exactly once, CSS brace balance, _ui_theme lints over panel.css, no .py under scripts/ui

outcome.technical: UI_HTML's 3,765-line r-string split programmatically at the <style>/<script> seams into ui/panel.{html,css,js} (31/823/2913 lines); _panel_ui.raw_template() reassembles at import (utf-8, module-global cache) and panel-server assigns UI_HTML from it with the .replace() chain untouched. Post-substitution UI_HTML proven byte-identical old-vs-new via importlib (244588 == 244588). panel-server 8287 -> 4521 lines; 23 new _panel_ui cases incl. mutation-proven exactly-once markers; scripts/ui pinned .py-free.
outcome.descriptive: The panel's CSS and JS are real files now, assembled byte-identically at import - every pin passed untouched and the served page is unchanged.

tasks.title: Report: ui/report.{css,js} + _report_ui
tasks.description: _report_ui exposes CSS (= _ui_theme.TOKEN_CSS + file) and SCRIPT; render-report assigns _CSS/_SCRIPT from it so all ~109 pins pass unchanged. Same logic-free-move rule as P11.1.

add: _report_ui: utf-8 decodability, brace balance, _ui_theme lints, no .py under ui/

outcome.technical: _CSS's plain-string part and _SCRIPT moved to ui/report.{css,js} (804/760 lines) behind _report_ui.py, which mirrors _panel_ui's conventions (tags added in Python, TOKEN_CSS concat stays Python-side). Extraction via ast.parse Constant.value after a naive text-slice was caught missing Python's escape processing on the non-raw _CSS literal. Byte-identity proven old-vs-new (61698==61698, 37708==37708). render-report 4587 -> 3024 lines; 17 _report_ui cases; check-report-interactive 47/47 on a fresh dogfood render.
outcome.descriptive: The report's CSS and JS are real files too, byte-identical in the rendered page, which stays one self-contained interactive document.

tasks.title: Guards + docs for the asset layout
tasks.description: The "scripts/ui holds no .py" invariant gets its pinned selftest case (a .py there would silently escape the flat CI selftest glob and the entries_missing_guard listdir). PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE and CONTRIBUTING body text updated to describe assembly-at-import — body text only, never headings, so _help.source_drift keeps resolving every citation.

outcome.technical: Both extraction modules already pinned scripts/ui .py-free (no code change needed). PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE's tree and two per-file prose sections now describe assembly-at-import; CONTRIBUTING gains the flat-layout hard rule with the scripts/ui exception; plugin README needed nothing - its self-containment claims are about the served page and remain true. No headings touched; drift lints green.
outcome.descriptive: The docs describe the new layout truthfully, and the flat-Python invariant is a written contributor rule instead of an accident.
